newsitem.title: GERMANY: World tourism fair opens with environment worries.
newsitem.headline: World tourism fair opens with environment worries.

text.p: Environmental ministers from 20 countries called on Saturday for tourism to be curbed in ecologically and culturally sensitive areas.
Participants in an international travel trade fair opening here on Saturday, their "Berlin Declaration" urged countries to train travel industry workers about the environment.
They called for restrictions on motorised safaris and protection of small islands, beaches and coral reefs.

"We cannot overburden the natural environment," said German Environmental Minister Angela Merkel at a news conference. She also said European Union environmental ministers want to introduce a tax on jet fuel.
Francesco Francialli, director of the World Tourism Organisation, said the number of tourist arrivals will nearly treble from 593 million in 1996 to 1.6 billion in 2020.
"The numbers will keep risising and we need to be more diligent in protecting the environment from tourism," he said. "The problems are going to get worse."

The 31st annual International Tourism Exchange (ITB) brings together exhibitors from 177 countries and expects more than 50,000 travel industry professionals along with another 70,000 visitors to attend the four-day exhibition.

Worldwide tourism revenues expanded to a record $423 billion in 1996 and in Germany alone turnover last year was 200 billion marks ($120 billion), making it the country's fifth most important sector and its leading service industry branch.
France leads the world as the most popular tourist destination while the United States had the highest tourism revenue. Spain, Italy and China rounded out the top five worldwide destinations.
The growth of tourism to China has accelerated in recent years, with the country moving from 25th position based on arrivals six years ago to fifth last year.

Eastern European countries such as Hungary and Poland continued to record strong growth and were the world's eighth and ninth favourite destinations last year with 21 and 19 million foreign visitors respectively.
